definitions: M_p^λ uses geometric mean at0,min at−∞,max at∞, and continuous zero conventions; all ratios are restricted to positive input supports.
The source p is the negative of the classical BBL interpolation exponent α; Q_d uses a minus sign denominator.

theorem_cards.label: Theorems1.2–1.3
assumptions: d≥1 integer; finitely many inputs m≥1; λ_i>0 and Σλ_i=1.
All f_i,g_i:R^d→R≥0 are Lebesgue measurable and integrable; 0<||f_i||1<∞.
S=∏{f_i>0}; evaluate ratios only on S, using Lebesgue essential infimum there.
p∈[−∞,1/d]; weighted power means follow Definition1.1 including zero and infinite-power conventions.
theorem_cards.statement: For K=essinf_(x∈S) M_p^λ(g_i(Σλ_jx_j)/f_i(x_i)), K≤M_(Q_d(p))^λ(||g_i||1/||f_i||1). Q_d(p)=p/(1−dp), Q_d(−∞)=−1/d, Q_d(1/d)=+∞. Common output gives classical BBL with α=−p≥−1/d and output exponent α/(1+dα), including −∞ at α=−1/d and 1/d at α=∞.
proof_steps: One-dimensional minimum inequality is built by merging two functions with normalized weights; preserve equal essential L∞ heights and propagate a.e. inequalities using an invertible linear map and Fubini.
Normalize bounded inputs to equal L∞ heights, compare min inputs to a weighted-power output, then apply reverse Minkowski for power≤1 and weighted Hölder.
Apply lower-dimensional results to slices, exclude null sets by Fubini and surjectivity of the output linear map, and combine Q_e(Q_d(p))=Q_(d+e)(p).
Extend unbounded inputs through truncation and monotone convergence; handle zero K separately.
theorem_cards.author_claim: For K=essinf_(x∈S) M_p^λ(g_i(Σλ_jx_j)/f_i(x_i)), K≤M_(Q_d(p))^λ(||g_i||1/||f_i||1). Q_d(p)=p/(1−dp), Q_d(−∞)=−1/d, Q_d(1/d)=+∞. Common output gives classical BBL with α=−p≥−1/d and output exponent α/(1+dα), including −∞ at α=−1/d and 1/d at α=∞.

theorem_cards.label: Remark2.10 and low-power proof limit
assumptions: m≥2; λ_i>0 summing1; measurable nonnegative integrable h_i.
Reverse Minkowski applies only to weighted power p≤1.
theorem_cards.statement: ∫M_p^λ(h_1,…,h_m)≤M_p^λ(∫h_1,…,∫h_m) for p≤1; it fails for p>1. Accordingly, derivation of multi-output BBL from classical BBL by this route is limited to p≤1/(d+1), although the new theorem itself extends to p≤1/d.
proof_steps: For pairwise disjoint E_i each of measure1, set h_i=1_Ei. For1<p<∞ left=Σλ_i^(1/p)>1=right; at p=∞ left=m.
Q_d(p)≤1 iff p≤1/(d+1); do not apply reverse Minkowski past this condition.
theorem_cards.author_claim: ∫M_p^λ(h_1,…,h_m)≤M_p^λ(∫h_1,…,∫h_m) for p≤1; it fails for p>1. Accordingly, derivation of multi-output BBL from classical BBL by this route is limited to p≤1/(d+1), although the new theorem itself extends to p≤1/d.

theorem_cards.label: Corollary7.1
assumptions: All Theorem1.3 hypotheses; real β_i≠0, without positivity or sum1 requirement.
Keep original λ as the weight in the power mean.
theorem_cards.statement: With output argument Σβ_i x_i, K_β≤M_(Q_d(p))^λ((λ_i/|β_i|)^d ||g_i||1/||f_i||1).
proof_steps: Set f_i♯(x)=f_i(λ_i x/β_i), whose integral is (|β_i|/λ_i)^d ||f_i||1.
The invertible input map preserves essential-infimum null sets and turns the output sum into the λ-weighted sum.
theorem_cards.author_claim: With output argument Σβ_i x_i, K_β≤M_(Q_d(p))^λ((λ_i/|β_i|)^d ||g_i||1/||f_i||1).

reusable_methods: Record the exact power convention and dimension transformation before passing to a marginal or slice.
Preserve a.e. quantifiers through invertible maps and Fubini; ordinary infimum and essential infimum are different.
Use slice induction with exact exponent composition, retaining finite positive input masses and output integrability.
